Company Overview

EKI Environment & Water, Inc. (EKI) is an employee-owned, full service, engineering and environmental sciences consulting firm serving private- and public-sector clients throughout the United States. If you are interested in improving water management strategies and practices, improving the environment, and advancing your career, then EKI is the place for you.

The Water Resources Project Manager position reports to the Team Leader (TL) and is responsible for project management and technical oversight of high-impact projects with California clients from initial project planning through implementation. Projects include Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) compliance and implementation, groundwater basin characterization, development of water budgets and water accounting frameworks, litigation support, water supply planning, and more.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities

Your responsibilities may include, but will not be limited to the following:

Coordinate SGMA implementation for groundwater basins across multiple Groundwater Sustainability Agencies
Oversee hydrogeologic conceptual model development, water balances, numerical models, and projects and/or management actions deemed necessary by the client
Prepare well-written technical memorandums or reports and studies, including groundwater sustainability plans (GSPs), SGMA annual reports, and periodic evaluations of adopted GSPs
Point of Contact for client; coordinate and lead client meetings and related meetings and coordination with external parties
Plan, organize, and manage staff to deliver quality project work products on time and within budget
Prepare effective presentations that efficiently communicate complex technical concepts to a broad audience
Manage project schedules, budgets, invoice preparation, and monthly progress reports
Provide quality assurance and quality control on and review of project deliverables
Support business development, including client development, preparing proposals, and presenting at conferences
Other duties as required

Qualifications & Requirements

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Hydrology, Geology, Earth Sciences, Engineering, or related field; Master’s or PhD degree preferred

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Minimum of five (5) years of experience, with eight (8) or more years desirable for SGMA and related water resources projects
At least two (2) years of proven project management experience
Master's or PhD degree, and Professional Registration, or more than 12 years of demonstrated professional experience where Professional Registration is not available for degree, is desirable
Technical knowledge of SGMA, Groundwater Sustainability Plans, data management and visualization, ArcGIS, quantitative analysis (including numerical modeling), land subsidence, and technical writing
Knowledge of California groundwater and water planning regulations

Must have excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate and coordinate effectively with clients, subconsultants, regulatory agencies, and members of the public as may be necessary to accomplish assigned objectives

Notice To Third Party Agencies

Department of Food \& Agriculture

### **Job Description and Duties**


**Per CCR 249\.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**


Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) (SES) is responsible for overseeing the operations of the Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch Central Region Office in Fresno, California. The incumbent will be responsible for the supervision of Environmental Scientists that conduct environmental health inspections on dairy farms and milk processing plants, gather scientific data, research and investigate food safety hazards, test pasteurization equipment for proper operation and food safety controls, and provide analytical expertise and reports on specific food safety parameters on dairies, processing plants, haulers and other dairy food facilities, including those associated with possible illegal sales of substandard or unsafe dairy products to California consumers.  

  

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food \& Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!  

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The CDFA does not participate in E\-Verify for employment authorization purposes.


You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The duties of this position are primarily conducted indoors approximately 80% of the time. The incumbent has an office in the Central Regional Office located in Downtown Fresno. The office is furnished with all the necessary equipment for job performance and function.  

Incumbents must be able to establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted during the course of the work, work well under pressure, make appropriate decisions and recommendations, work independently to complete assignments and meet deadlines.  

When working outdoors the incumbent may be exposed to extremes in temperatures and high noise levels in a variety of environments ranging from individual dairy farm premises to complex, multi\-story processing plants complexes.  

Occasional travel (including nights and weekends) may be required for meetings, events, and field support as needed. A state issued vehicle may be assigned to drive on state business.  

The incumbent must follow CDFA, Division, and Branch employee health and safety policies.  

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. While CDFA supports telework where possible, in\-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. Employees are expected to be able to report to their worksite with minimal notification if an urgent need arises, as determined by the Department.

The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.


The Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch is responsible for ensuring that milk, dairy products, and products resembling milk products (PRMP’s) are safe, unadulterated, and properly labeled to safeguard public health. The Branch inspects dairy farms, bulk milk tanker trucks, and milk processing plants; issues permits and licenses to dairy farms and processing facilities; collects samples for regulatory testing to ensure compliance with food safety and quality standards; reviews product labels for conformance with regulations to avoid misleading information for consumers; completes in\-depth reviews and food safety assessments of complex equipment or novel processing methods, and evaluates and licenses technical food safety competencies of dairy industry workers. The Branch also responds to food safety incidents, and initiates product impounds and recalls as warranted. $90k-$110k DOE

Responsibilities

LEADERSHIP AND DEPARTMENT MANAGEMENT

Manage equipment lifecycle activities in support of equipment calibration, validation, and PM activities
Support personnel training, qualifications, mentoring, workload planning, and development to ensure assigned duties are performed competently and consistently

jobs.description:
Company Overview

Pattern Energy is a leading renewable energy company that develops, constructs, owns, and operates high-quality wind and solar generation, transmission, and energy storage facilities. Our mission is to transition the world to renewable energy through the sustainable development and responsible operation of facilities with respect for the environment, communities, and cultures where we have a presence.

Our approach begins and ends with establishing trust, accountability, and transparency. Our company values of creative spirit, pride of ownership, follow-through, and a team-first attitude drive us to pursue our mission every day. Our culture supports our values by fostering innovative and critical thinking and a deep belief in living up to our promises.

Pattern Energy operates in the United States and Canada, with offices in San Francisco, Houston, San Diego, New York and Toronto. Pattern Energy Group's corporate headquarters are in San Francisco. Pattern has a global portfolio of more than 35 power facilities and transmission assets, serving various customers that provide low-cost clean energy to millions of consumers.

Responsibilities

JOB PURPOSE

The Manager, Environmental Compliance & Strategy, EPC is responsible for ensuring environmental compliance and supporting strategic risk planning for Pattern’s projects during execution, with a primary focus on wind, transmission, and solar energy projects in the United States and Canada, and ancillary support for compliance efforts in other jurisdictions as needed.

This role leads and coordinates environmental construction permit compliance activities, supports environmental compliance programs and tools, and works closely with internal project teams, consultants, contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups to ensure Pattern’s projects meet applicable environmental permit, regulatory, and internal compliance requirements.

To support ongoing Pattern projects, viable candidates may also be considered if they live near Pattern project locations in Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Louisiana, Montana, North Dakota, or New Mexico, as an optional work location arrangement.

Key Accountabilities

The key responsibilities will include as a minimum the following:

Lead environmental construction permit compliance activities in coordination with Pattern EPC group managers, engineering and construction managers, project construction contractors, and Pattern Environmental Development and Operations teams.
Manage and coordinate project environmental personnel, including environmental consultants, EPC and specialty contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups as appropriate.
Conduct environmental compliance reviews, participate in monthly management meetings, complete site audits, and support compliance root-cause analysis investigations and reviews.
Assist in the development and implementation of Pattern environmental compliance programs, procedures, and project execution documents.
Create, maintain, and update project environmental compliance matrices during project execution.
Develop and deliver Environmental Awareness Training for EPC and contractor staff.
Coordinate with federal, state, provincial, and local environmental agency leads to resolve environmental concerns during construction.
Budget for and manage consultants providing project-level environmental support services, including construction environmental monitoring and wildlife mitigation strategies.
Represent Pattern in industry organizations and technical committees, supporting benchmarking, collaboration, and thought leadership across the renewable energy sector.

Qualifications

Experience/Qualifications/Education Required

Educational Experience

A bachelor’s degree in a science-oriented field such as Biology, Ecology, Environmental Sciences, Wildlife, or a related field is required. An advanced degree in Law, Biology, Environmental Sciences, Ecology, or a comparable discipline is preferred.

Required Work Experience

The following criteria will be used as a basis for Pattern to select a qualified applicant:

Seven or more years of experience in environmental, natural resources, or energy-related projects, preferably in renewable energy.
Experience with wind, transmission, and/or solar power permitting, environmental construction compliance, and environmental fieldwork.
Familiarity with federal, state, and provincial environmental regulations related to stormwater, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, air quality, wildlife, archaeology, environmental due diligence, and associated compliance programs.
Extensive experience with stormwater best management practices, including design, implementation, maintenance, and cost considerations.
Experience collaborating with cross-functional project teams and managing environmental consultants and contractors.

Additional Requirements

Must possess strengths in the following:

Strong time management, diplomacy, and specialized environmental compliance knowledge.
Ability to make informed recommendations regarding the interpretation and application of environmental permits, regulations, and laws in evolving regulatory environments.
Ability to analyze, organize, and interpret data from multiple sources and translate findings into clear written deliverables.
Strong professional communication skills, including the ability to influence best practices and change within projects and the broader organization.
Ability to multi-task, adapt quickly, work well under pressure, collaborate in large teams and one-on-one settings, and work independently with minimal supervision.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, up to approximately 25%, depending on project needs.

Technical Skills

Computer skills – working knowledge of Windows-based business software applications, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

Environmental compliance – detailed knowledge of environmental regulatory frameworks, including wildlife, natural resources, stormwater, site restoration, spills, waste, audits, and project-specific permit or regulatory requirements for projects in the United States and/or Canada.

The expected starting pay range for this role is $103,000 - $138,000 USD. This range is an estimate and base pay may be above or below the ranges based on several factors including but not limited to location, work experience, certifications, and education. In addition to base pay, Pattern’s compensation program includes a bonus structure for full-time employees of all levels. We also provide a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, voluntary benefits, family care benefits, employee assistance program, paid time off and bonding leave, paid holidays, 401(k)/RRSP retirement savings plan with employer contribution, and employee referral bonuses.

Our approach begins and ends with establishing trust, accountability, and transparency. Our company values of creative spirit, pride of ownership, follow-through, and a team-first attitude drive us to pursue our mission every day. Our culture supports our values by fostering innovative and critical thinking and a deep belief in living up to our promises.

Pattern Energy operates in the United States and Canada, with offices in San Francisco, Houston, San Diego, New York and Toronto. Pattern Energy Group's corporate headquarters are in San Francisco. Pattern has a global portfolio of more than 35 power facilities and transmission assets, serving various customers that provide low-cost clean energy to millions of consumers.

Responsibilities

JOB PURPOSE

The Manager, Environmental Compliance & Strategy, EPC is responsible for ensuring environmental compliance and supporting strategic risk planning for Pattern’s projects during execution, with a primary focus on wind, transmission, and solar energy projects in the United States and Canada, and ancillary support for compliance efforts in other jurisdictions as needed.

This role leads and coordinates environmental construction permit compliance activities, supports environmental compliance programs and tools, and works closely with internal project teams, consultants, contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups to ensure Pattern’s projects meet applicable environmental permit, regulatory, and internal compliance requirements.

To support ongoing Pattern projects, viable candidates may also be considered if they live near Pattern project locations in Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Louisiana, Montana, North Dakota, or New Mexico, as an optional work location arrangement.

Key Accountabilities

The key responsibilities will include as a minimum the following:

Lead environmental construction permit compliance activities in coordination with Pattern EPC group managers, engineering and construction managers, project construction contractors, and Pattern Environmental Development and Operations teams.
Manage and coordinate project environmental personnel, including environmental consultants, EPC and specialty contractors, regulatory authorities, and local interest groups as appropriate.
Conduct environmental compliance reviews, participate in monthly management meetings, complete site audits, and support compliance root-cause analysis investigations and reviews.
Assist in the development and implementation of Pattern environmental compliance programs, procedures, and project execution documents.
Create, maintain, and update project environmental compliance matrices during project execution.
Develop and deliver Environmental Awareness Training for EPC and contractor staff.
Coordinate with federal, state, provincial, and local environmental agency leads to resolve environmental concerns during construction.
Budget for and manage consultants providing project-level environmental support services, including construction environmental monitoring and wildlife mitigation strategies.
Represent Pattern in industry organizations and technical committees, supporting benchmarking, collaboration, and thought leadership across the renewable energy sector.

Qualifications

Experience/Qualifications/Education Required

Educational Experience

A bachelor’s degree in a science-oriented field such as Biology, Ecology, Environmental Sciences, Wildlife, or a related field is required. An advanced degree in Law, Biology, Environmental Sciences, Ecology, or a comparable discipline is preferred.

Required Work Experience

The following criteria will be used as a basis for Pattern to select a qualified applicant:

Seven or more years of experience in environmental, natural resources, or energy-related projects, preferably in renewable energy.
Experience with wind, transmission, and/or solar power permitting, environmental construction compliance, and environmental fieldwork.
Familiarity with federal, state, and provincial environmental regulations related to stormwater, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, air quality, wildlife, archaeology, environmental due diligence, and associated compliance programs.
Extensive experience with stormwater best management practices, including design, implementation, maintenance, and cost considerations.
Experience collaborating with cross-functional project teams and managing environmental consultants and contractors.

Additional Requirements

Must possess strengths in the following:

Strong time management, diplomacy, and specialized environmental compliance knowledge.
Ability to make informed recommendations regarding the interpretation and application of environmental permits, regulations, and laws in evolving regulatory environments.
Ability to analyze, organize, and interpret data from multiple sources and translate findings into clear written deliverables.
Strong professional communication skills, including the ability to influence best practices and change within projects and the broader organization.
Ability to multi-task, adapt quickly, work well under pressure, collaborate in large teams and one-on-one settings, and work independently with minimal supervision.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, up to approximately 25%, depending on project needs.

Technical Skills

Computer skills – working knowledge of Windows-based business software applications, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

Environmental compliance – detailed knowledge of environmental regulatory frameworks, including wildlife, natural resources, stormwater, site restoration, spills, waste, audits, and project-specific permit or regulatory requirements for projects in the United States and/or Canada.

The expected starting pay range for this role is $103,000 - $138,000 USD. This range is an estimate and base pay may be above or below the ranges based on several factors including but not limited to location, work experience, certifications, and education. In addition to base pay, Pattern’s compensation program includes a bonus structure for full-time employees of all levels. We also provide a comprehensive benefits package which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, life insurance, voluntary benefits, family care benefits, employee assistance program, paid time off and bonding leave, paid holidays, 401(k)/RRSP retirement savings plan with employer contribution, and employee referral bonuses.

jobs.title: Principal Air Quality Chemist
jobs.description:
South Coast Aqmd And Job Overview

ABOUT SOUTH COAST AQMD

South Coast Air Quality Management District (South Coast AQMD) is one of the largest and most technologically sophisticated environmental regulatory agencies in the nation, serving a four-county region that includes Los Angeles, Orange County, Riverside and San Bernardino counties, and the Coachella Valley. South Coast AQMD's headquarters is located in Diamond Bar, 30 miles east of downtown Los Angeles, at the junction of the 57 and 60 Freeways. With a highly diverse "Clean Air Team" of over 870 employees, an annual budget of $225.2 million, and a state-of-the art air quality laboratory, our mission is to ensure clean air and a healthy environment. South Coast AQMD is an organization you can be proud to work for -- we make a difference in the quality of life in Southern California!

South Coast AQMD is committed to creating and maintaining a work environment that appreciates the unique backgrounds, skills, and experiences of our employees and fosters professional development and growth. South Coast AQMD respects the ideas and perspectives of our stakeholders and works to bring them together toward the common goal of clean air.

About Our Laboratory

South Coast AQMD's laboratory employs over 40 staff in a 20,000 square foot state-of-the-art facility dedicated to air quality sample analysis. It provides a broad array of services generating actionable data that is used for strategic planning, investigating complaints from the community, evaluating new products and processes, supporting incident responses and determining compliance with regulations. We also provide data to the California Air Resources Board, US EPA, law enforcement agencies, and universities. Results generated by the laboratory have been the catalyst for agency-wide policy decisions, special studies, and technology development. We analyze over 60,000 samples per year using various analytical laboratory techniques; including GC, IC, LC, GC-MS, XRF, XRD, FTIR, microscopic analysis, ICP-MS, and PTR-MS to generate detailed information on the types and amount of pollutants in ambient air. The South Coast AQMD laboratory is at the forefront of method development for ambient air analyses and obtains national recognition in the field of air quality analytical chemistry.

About This Position

The South Coast AQMD is seeking qualified candidates to fill a Principal Air Quality Chemist vacancy. From this recruitment process, we expect to establish an eligible list from which current and future vacancies may be filled, during the 6–12-month life of the list.

Principal Chemists are expected to have expertise in many analytical techniques, data analysis, and to supervise the work of staff in their respective group. Therefore, the most competitive candidates for this position will bring a strong combination of education, atmospheric and analytical chemistry training and experience, broad knowledge of QA/QC procedures, and supervisory skills and readiness. This position will be responsible for oversight of the South Coast AQMD laboratory's Advanced Spectrometry and Microscopy groups. The primary role of the Advanced Spectrometry Principal Chemist is to help with community monitoring needs under several South Coast AQMD programs, including AB 617 (Community Air Toxics Monitoring), incident response, rule development and support, and special monitoring projects using a mobile Proton-Transfer-Reaction-Time-of-Flight-Mass Spectrometer (PTR-MS) and other advanced instrumentation.

The Principal Air Quality Chemist is a supervisory position reporting to the Laboratory Manager. This vacant position is one of four Principal positions making up the laboratory supervisory team; each team consists of eight to sixteen chemists, technicians, and support staff. Teams are aligned by function, including compliance analysis, ambient VOC/toxics analysis, aerosol analysis, and advanced spectrometry/microscopy.

EXAMPLE OF DUTIES

The general Example of Duties for this classification are highlighted below, for full description of duties please refer to this link here .

Plans, organizes, and supervises the work of staff assigned to a laboratory section involved in qualitative and quantitative analyses to isolate, identify, and quantify air contaminants; reviews requests for analyses, determines the level of difficulty, and assigns work; and provides technical and administrative guidance to professional and technical staff and evaluates performance.
Develops, supervises, prioritizes, and evaluates programs and projects; maintains workload statistics on unit activities; prepares program- and activity-related reports and analyses; reviews and edits technical reports prepared by laboratory staff to ensure accuracy of data, appropriateness of methodologies, and soundness of findings and conclusions; and identifies and maintains data quality objectives on a program basis.
Serves as a technical expert and resource for South Coast AQMD staff regarding chemistry-related air quality matters and on a variety of technical advisory committees; maintains a broad understanding of current research into causes, sources, and chemical reactions contributing to air quality problems; and consults with outside experts regarding air quality issues relevant to laboratory programs and projects.
Applies professional training and experience and keeps abreast of updated and new chemical laboratory methods, instrumentation, protocols, and practices through review of professional literature and other research resources and evaluates staff recommendations to ensure the laboratory uses the most effective and up-to-date techniques in analyzing air contaminants, accomplishing the work of the unit, and meeting new or changing South Coast AQMD rules.
Reviews and approves test methods used by private laboratories for compliance with South Coast AQMD rules.
Represents South Coast AQMD at scientific conferences and prepares for publication and presents research reports and papers on methods, procedures, results, and conclusions relating to laboratory analyses.
Testifies in court and before public bodies and hearing boards.
Prepares annual budget request for the section and submits written justification for budget items requested; and is responsible for the preparation of grant proposals for federal government or other funding.
Acts for the laboratory services manager, as needed.

Desirable Qualifications

MINIMUM AND DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

In addition to the Minimum Qualifications which follow, the most competitive candidates will also possess:

Experience with the measurement of Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) in ambient air, and the analysis, interpretation, and presentation of resultant data sets.
Experience with mobile measurements and/or field studies using research grade instrumentation, particularly mass spectrometry techniques such as PTR-MS and spectroscopic methods such as CRDS and TILDAS; along with other analytical techniques for the measurement of ambient gases and particles.
Experience with microscopic analysis for asbestos and other ambient particulate matter using polarized light microscopy, electron microscopy with EDS, XRD, FTIR, and other techniques.
Knowledge of QA/QC procedures and guidelines to ensure data is accurate and representative of the samples being collected following proper documentation procedures.
Detailed knowledge of matters directly related to ambient air analysis, laboratory instrumentation and data management.
Exceptional leadership, oral presentation, and written communication skills.
Experience overseeing the work of laboratory professionals and support staff.
Ability to identify and resolve complex programmatic and administrative challenges in a fair, impartial, and professional manner.
Ability to implement and track the progress of programs and innovative solutions to improve efficiency and productivity.
Ability to conceptualize mobile monitoring and field data using GIS based visualizations.
Ability to manage workloads to ensure timely turnaround of sample analysis and data collected during field measurements.
Ability to lead teams operating field instrumentation, both stationary and mobile, that is used extensively for monitoring pollutants near facilities and in nearby communities as well as for incident response.
Ability to oversee contracts for monitoring studies along with collaborating with researchers at universities and other agencies.
Ability to present technical data to various stakeholders having a wide range of scientific and professional backgrounds.
Strong computer and data review skills for large complex datasets that harmonize data from several instruments often with different time resolutions.
Flexibility, dependability, and a positive, can-do attitude.

Minimum Qualifications

EDUCATION:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree in chemistry, preferably with an emphasis in qualitative and quantitative analysis.

Experience

One (1) year as a Senior Air Quality Chemist or equivalent (One year working as a Manager, Supervisor, Senior Chemist, or similar leadership position that oversees a group of chemists focused on air quality measurements and/or research) OR
Three (3) years as an Air Quality Chemist or equivalent (Three years working as a Chemist conducting air quality analysis).

KNOWLEDGE OF:
Current methods, procedures, protocols, and instrumentation relating to organic, inorganic, and physical qualitative and quantitative analysis; operational principles of relevant chemical laboratory instrumentation and techniques; principles and practices of project management, supervision, training, and budgeting; relevant professional research literature and resources; principles and methods of statistical analysis; working knowledge of database design, information management, and computer programming, as they relate to laboratory analysis of air contaminants; safety procedures and practices relating to laboratory work; PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; professional report writing; South Coast AQMD rules and federal and State laws related to chemical analysis of air contaminants; and protocols and standards for laboratory analysis of air quality samples.

SKILL OR ABILITY TO:
Supervise, evaluate, train, and assign work to professional and technical staff involved in routine and complex qualitative and quantitative organic, inorganic and physical analysis of air quality samples; effectively use available resources in planning and organizing programs and projects; evaluate the effectiveness of programs and projects in meeting laboratory and overall South Coast AQMD objectives; oversee the development and implementation of new laboratory methods, procedures, and protocols, the adaptation of existing instrumentation and methods for new purposes, and the evaluation of new instrumentation; understand and interpret applicable laws, rules, and regulations; edit and write detailed, accurate reports on laboratory projects, analyses, methodologies, findings, and conclusions; prepare funding proposals; read, understand, and follow verbal and written directions; proficiently use PC software applications common to the field and to the general business environment of South Coast AQMD; communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing; and establish and maintain effective relationships with all those contacted in the course of work.

LICENSE:
Possession of a valid California Class "C" Driver's License and a good driving record may be required.

Other Important Information

APPLICATION PACKETS MUST INCLUDE

A completed employment application covering at least the past 10 years of employment history (or longer if you have other relevant experience), and your entire South Coast AQMD employment history if you are a South Coast AQMD employee.

The Earth and Environmental Sciences Department in the College of Natural Sciences is collecting application materials for a pool of lecturers with positions available as determined by need during the 2026-27 academic year. Appointments from the lecturer pool are temporary and often made just prior to the start of the academic term.

Preferred Qualifications

Faculty and students are actively involved in internal and external research grants and service contracts, and the University and College offer funding to support development of innovative student-learning techniques for both field and in-class activities. jobs.title: Senior Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
The Senior Environmental Health & Safety Specialist
protects employees, customers, visitors, property, and assets from injury or loss. Ensures compliance with pertinent regulations and the Global EHS Policy.

Essential Functions:

Leads and supports compliance efforts related to Local, State, and Federal Environmental, Health & Safety regulations and standards. Acts as a liaison with regulatory agencies, submits required regulatory reports in a timely manner, and ensures ongoing compliance with permits and applicable regulations.
Conducts site and machine risk assessments, job hazard analyses, industrial hygiene surveys, and compliance audits to identify hazards, evaluate risk exposure, and recommend corrective actions for manufacturing equipment, processes, and operational activities.
Facilitates safety representative meetings across all shifts to communicate Environmental, Health & Safety initiatives, review trends, discuss concerns, and promote employee engagement in safety programs.
Develops, implements, updates, and maintains site-specific Environmental, Health & Safety programs, policies, procedures, and training materials to support regulatory compliance and continuous improvement initiatives.
Assists with Workers’ Compensation claims administration and provides all necessary documentation for investigations and claim management. Coordinates communication between the third-party administrator, medical providers, supervisors, and employees regarding return-to-work plans and work restrictions.
Responds to emergencies, injuries, workplace violence incidents, spills, etc. Performs post-incident and hazard investigations to determine root causes and implement corrective and preventive actions to reduce future risk.
Ensures the safe handling, storage, transportation, and disposal of hazardous chemicals and waste materials. Defines HAZWOPER activities, coordinates required training, maintains chemical inventories and Safety Data Sheets (SDS), and ensures appropriate supplies and equipment are available.
Reviews Lockout/Tagout procedures annually and conducts periodic audits to verify procedures are accurate, effective, and consistently followed throughout operations.
Conducts routine safety inspections of manufacturing, warehouse, tooling, maintenance, and office areas to identify unsafe conditions, ensure compliance, and track corrective actions to completion.
Maintains OSHA logs, inspection records, training records, and other Environmental, Health & Safety documentation required for regulatory compliance and internal reporting through our EHS Data Management System.
Tracks, manages, and maintains site-specific Environmental, Health & Safety projects and action items through our project management system to ensure timely completion
Partners with Engineering, Maintenance, Production, and Facilities teams to support safe equipment installations, process changes, and continuous improvement projects.
Assists with contractor safety activities including onboarding requirements, documentation review, and monitoring compliance with site safety expectations.
Supports environmental compliance activities including stormwater inspections, hazardous waste management, and environmental reporting requirements.

Education/Training Required and Preferred:

Bachelor’s degree in related field, or a combination of education and relevant work experience.
Certified Safety Professional (CSP) and/or Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) preferred.
HAZMAT AND HAZWOPER certifications preferred.
Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and First-Aid certifications. Automated External Defibrillator (AED) certification preferred.

Experience Required and Preferred:

Minimum five years of experience working in the Environmental Health and Safety field, preferably in Manufacturing.

What You Bring:

Knowledge of safety and environmental regulations and related state and federal laws, as well as experience in interacting with regulatory agencies required. Experience working with state and federal regulations relating to Air Pollution Control District (APCD), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and California Occupational Safety and Health Administration (Cal-OSHA) required.
Knowledge and experience working with the principles of accident prevention and safety required.
Experience in ergonomics and performing ergonomic evaluations required.
Ability to lead a team, influence without authority and display effective project management skills required.
Strong knowledge of Microsoft Office programs required. Experience with MSDSOnline, VelocityEHS and Aha preferred.
Excellent attention to detail and prioritization skills required.
Ability to make mathematical calculations and operate various office equipment required.
Ability to self-initiate activities and work within timelines required. Must be flexible and able to adapt to changing organizational needs. Ability to work with minimal direction.
Knowledge of principles and techniques of employee training required.
Ability to make sound judgments and respond to emergency situations in a calm manner required.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English required.
Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to interface with members across the organization required.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally to support Environmental Health and Safety needs at additional office locations preferred. Must have or be able to obtain a valid passport.
Forklift driving experience preferred.
Ability to speak and write in Spanish preferred.

Job Description And Duties

The Enforcement Division’s (ED) Vehicle Enforcement Section (VES) is seeking a highly qualified and motivated Air Pollution Specialist (APS). The Vehicle Enforcement Section is responsible for enforcing CARB regulations designed to improve air quality by reducing emissions generated by (1) non-compliant on-road vehicles, including cars, trucks, motorcycles, and kit cars, and (2) non-compliant off-highway recreational vehicles, including all-terrain vehicles, sand rails, sand cars, utility carts, golf carts, dirt bikes, and other off-highway recreational vehicles with greater than 25-horsepower engines, and new pleasure craft engines and vehicles.

Enforcement services provided by VES focus primarily on investigating complaints, tips, and leads concerning potentially non-compliant vehicles, parts, specialty products, and laboratory and certification fraud, initiating enforcement actions where violations are found, and resolving these cases, including providing support in cases that are referred for litigation.

Occasionally, the incumbent will coordinate and collaborate with other CARB Divisions, other agencies, such as the Environmental Protection Agency, California Attorney General's Office, or the Department of Justice, to further inspections and/or investigations. The incumbent will participate in the review and interpretation of air pollution regulation requirements to determine potential emission sources for inspection and/or investigation. The incumbent will research and prepare technical reports, correspondence, or documentation relating to enforcement action taken to correct noncompliance and provide support in cases that are referred for litigation to a local district attorney or the Attorney General’s Office. jobs.description:
**Position Description:** 

The Academic Remediation Specialist is a licensed Registered Nurse (RN) who supports Vocational Nursing students in achieving academic and clinical competency. This role provides targeted tutoring, skills instruction, and simulation lab support to assist students in mastering course content, clinical skills, and critical thinking. The Academic Remediation Specialist ensures all remediation efforts align with the California Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians (BVNPT) requirements and Summit. On site position. Regular Reliable Attendance. Teaching as needed.

**Essential Functions:**

* Provide individualized and group tutoring sessions for nursing students to strengthen understanding of lecture content and address areas of difficulty.
* Collaborate with nursing faculty to align tutoring materials with course objectives and BVNPT\-approved curriculum.
* Develop and implement study strategies and tools tailored to diverse learning styles and academic needs.
* Facilitate skills lab remediation sessions, offering guidance and practice opportunities to build clinical competencies.
* Provide training and support for instructors on simulation\-based teaching methods, ensuring alignment with BVNPT standards and program objectives.
* Conduct structured simulation scenarios to reinforce critical thinking, clinical judgment, and technical skills in a safe, controlled environment.
* Maintain simulation equipment inventory and ensure software is updated and functioning properly, including troubleshooting as needed.
* Serve as the lead for simulation software management, maintaining vendor and IT communication to ensure functionality, compliance, and continuous improvement of simulation resource
* Assess student performance during remediation sessions and provide constructive feedback for improvement.
* Monitor student progress and identify recurring academic or clinical challenges requiring additional support.
* Maintain detailed records of remediation activities, student attendance, and progress to ensure compliance with BVNPT and institutional standards.
* Collaborate with faculty to track student outcomes on LMS/SIS and develop individualized remediation plans as needed.
* Serve as a liaison between students and faculty to ensure seamless communication and alignment of remediation efforts with course objectives.
* Participate in departmental meetings, workshops, and professional development activities to remain current with best practices in simulation, nursing education and remediation.
* Assist in developing and updating remediation policies, procedures, and resources to meet evolving BVNPT and institutional requirements.
* Gather, interpret, and communicate ATI assessment results to guide remediation planning, strengthen NCLEX preparation, and support continuous program improvement.
* Facilitate and oversee Term 4 exit procedures, assisting students with forms, Financial Aid exit, graduation clearance, Livescan, and NCLEX contract to ensure a seamless transition to licensure eligibility.
* Oversee and document NCLEX testing and licensure payment activities, ensuring accurate tracking, compliance with institutional policies, and timely student submissions.
* Organize and coordinate student CPR class \& other recertifications as necessary.
* Create and maintain student files as per BVNPT compliance.
* Provide substitute instructor coverage as needed by teaching theory or clinical.
* Take an active role in advisory board meetings, providing program updates, collecting feedback, and ensuring alignment with BVNPT and industry standards.
* Peer Training and Projects assigned by Management/DON
* Perform other duties as assigned

**Licensure/Education/ Work Experience Requirements:**

* RN License active in CA; Baccalaureate degree or valid teaching credential or a minimum of one year of fulltime teaching experience in a state approved registered nursing or vocational or practical nursing or psychiatric technician within the last five years or met community college or state university teaching requirements in California; and have a minimum of two years of experience as a Registered Nurse within the last five years
* Demonstrated proficiency with ATI software, curriculum alignment, and analytics to track student outcomes, identify risk factors, and support BVNPT compliance.
* BLS certification required; additional certifications (e.g., ACLS, PALS) preferred.
* Minimum of three (3\) years of clinical nursing experience required.
* Previous experience in nursing education, tutoring, or clinical instruction preferred.
* Strong knowledge of BVNPT standards and nursing curricula.
* Proficiency with simulation equipment and clinical skills training tools.
* Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
* Ability to work effectively with diverse student populations and collaborate with faculty and staff.

Qualifications

To qualify for an Environmental Protection Specialist, your resume and supporting documentation must support:

A: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is typically in or related to the position to be filled. To qualify at the GS-11 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military or private sector. To qualify at the GS-09 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military or private sector. Gs-09

Gs-11

GS-11: A Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M., if related.

C. Combination: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements for grade levels GS-11 and GS-09, and may be computed by first determining the applicant's total qualifying experience as a percentage of the experience required for the grade level; then determining the applicant's education as a percentage of the education required for the grade level; and then adding the two percentages. The total percentages must equal at least 100 percent to qualify an applicant for that grade level. Excellent problem-solving abilities

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Enforcement Division’s (ED) Vehicle Enforcement Section (VES) is seeking a highly qualified and motivated Air Pollution Specialist (APS). The Vehicle Enforcement Section is responsible for enforcing CARB regulations designed to improve air quality by reducing emissions generated by (1\) non\-compliant on\-road vehicles, including cars, trucks, motorcycles, and kit cars, and (2\) non\-compliant off\-highway recreational vehicles, including all\-terrain vehicles, sand rails, sand cars, utility carts, golf carts, dirt bikes, and other off\-highway recreational vehicles with greater than 25\-horsepower engines, and new pleasure craft engines and vehicles.  

Enforcement services provided by VES focus primarily on investigating complaints, tips, and leads concerning potentially non\-compliant vehicles, parts, specialty products, and laboratory and certification fraud, initiating enforcement actions where violations are found, and resolving these cases, including providing support in cases that are referred for litigation.  

Occasionally, the incumbent will coordinate and collaborate with other CARB Divisions, other agencies, such as the Environmental Protection Agency, California Attorney General's Office, or the Department of Justice, to further inspections and/or investigations. The incumbent will participate in the review and interpretation of air pollution regulation requirements to determine potential emission sources for inspection and/or investigation. The incumbent will research and prepare technical reports, correspondence, or documentation relating to enforcement action taken to correct noncompliance and provide support in cases that are referred for litigation to a local district attorney or the Attorney General’s Office. * Comprehensive understanding of Australian Standards and water legislation, environmental regulations, and compliance requirements

* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills for both technical and non\-technical audience

Job Posting: Senior Staff Biologist



California Energy Commission


JC\-527490* 

Senior Staff Biologist
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SPECIALIST)
$7,820\.00 \- $10,732\.00 per Month  

  



**Final Filing Date:** **8/26/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


Under the general direction of the Biological Resources Unit Supervisor, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) will serve as a lead scientific expert for biological resources and natural resources conservation associated with the certification, environmental review, and compliance verification of the most highly complex and extremely sensitive energy facility projects, policy, and planning studies in accordance with the Warren\-Alquist Act and the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). The Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) is a subject matter expert and independently plans and conducts complex, critical environmental evaluations; reviews and interprets biological surveys, studies, and reports; conducts technical research; assesses potential impacts to species and habitats; and develops mitigation measures, monitoring requirements, and recommendations. The Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) formulates and develops solutions to extremely difficult and controversial issues on a wide range of projects.
  

  

The Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) prepares technically accurate environmental analyses, communicates complex scientific information to technical and non\-technical audiences, and works collaboratively with agencies, stakeholders, industry representatives, consultants, and multidisciplinary teams to resolve complex environmental issues. The Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) may also act as a working team leader or as a lead person over a group of technical specialists or on the most complex projects.
  

  

**Minimum Qualifications (MQs):** The MQs for this classification can be found at Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist).The documents you submit in your application package must highlight how you meet the MQs. If the MQs are not met, you will not be considered for this position.
  

  

**Education Information:** If you are using education to meet the minimum qualifications for this classification, please provide your unofficial transcripts. Applicants who completed their education outside of the United States (with foreign degrees/transcripts) must provide evaluated transcripts. The transcript evaluation must state the number of units to which foreign coursework is equal. Foreign education evaluation services can be found at https://www.naces.org.Official transcripts and official foreign degree transcripts will be required prior to appointment. If you are not using education to qualify for this classification, you do not need to submit transcripts. To bypass the required document, select Choose/Upload and select Bypass File.

  

  

Please let us know how you heard about this position by taking a brief survey at CEC Recruitment Survey.


You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The CEC supports a hybrid workplace model with office\-based and remote\-centered workers. Limited in\-person attendance and occasional travel may be required based on the needs of the division. Regular and consistent attendance is essential to successful performance. This position is remote\-centered, which means the incumbent works 50 percent or more of their time from an alternate work location. Teleworking is only available for employees who reside in California. You must be located in California and provide your in\-state address prior to your start date.

The CEC was established by the Legislature in 1974 to address energy challenges facing the state. Today, the CEC is the state's primary energy policy and planning agency and is leading the state to a 100% clean energy future. Serving all Californians, the CEC embodies diversity, equity, and inclusion, and has taken an active and meaningful role in creating an environment that enables each employee to thrive. The CEC operates under the umbrella of the California Natural Resources Agency and shares offices with the agency in a LEED Platinum Certified Building in downtown Sacramento.
  

  

The California Energy Commission seeks a Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) in the Siting, Transmission and Environmental Protection Division / Siting and Environmental Branch / Biological Resources Unit. If you are interested in a challenging and exciting career in clean energy and are passionate about renewable, efficient, and reliable energy that addresses climate change, join our diverse team of global energy leaders! The California Energy Commission plays a lead role in creating the energy system of the future, not just in California, but globally. This position is open to interested applicants who qualify. 2\) Complete Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) exam and pass the to be eligible to be hired for available positions. See information on Energy Commission Assessments and Exams.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**Senior Environmental Scientist**

 **Senior Environmental Scientist**


**Brisbane or Cairns QLD**


RPS, A Tetra Tech company


RPS, A Tetra Tech company, is a global professional services firm delivering projects that define, shape and manage Australia's most important infrastructure, development and environmental initiatives.


With more than 5,000 professionals across 125 countries, we bring together technical excellence, practical thinking and a collaborative approach to solve complex challenges across infrastructure, energy, water, environment, urban development and resources.


Our Oceans \& Environment team partners with government and private sector clients to deliver innovative environmental solutions that support sustainable development while protecting our natural environment.


**The Opportunity**


Due to continued growth, we are looking for a Senior Environmental Scientist to join our Oceans \& Environment team in our Brisbane or Cairns offices.


This is an exciting opportunity to work on a diverse portfolio of infrastructure, renewable energy, transport, water and development projects across Queensland and Australia. You will collaborate with experienced environmental consultants and technical specialists to deliver environmental assessments, approvals and management solutions that help clients achieve successful project outcomes.


Whether you enjoy field work, technical reporting, environmental approvals or working closely with clients, this role offers excellent variety and the opportunity to grow your career within a supportive national team.


**What You Will Be Doing**


* Preparing environmental assessments, technical reports and environmental management plans.
* Assisting with environmental impact assessments and planning approval documentation.
* Conducting environmental investigations, literature reviews and data analysis.
* Supporting environmental approvals under Queensland and Commonwealth legislation.
* Coordinating inputs from technical specialists and project stakeholders.
* Working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
* Building strong relationships with clients, regulators and internal stakeholders.
* Assisting with project planning, budgeting and delivery to meet client expectations.
* Supporting proposal preparation and business development activities.
* Ensuring work is delivered safely on time and to a high technical standard.


**About You**


You will be passionate about delivering practical environmental outcomes and enjoy working on a wide variety of projects in a collaborative consulting environment.


You will also bring:


* A degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
* Experience working in environmental consulting, government or a related industry.
* Knowledge of Queensland environmental legislation and environmental assessment processes.
* An understanding of the Commonwealth Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (EPBC Act).
* Strong technical report writing and communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex information clearly.
* Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
* A collaborative approach and a commitment to delivering quality outcomes for clients.
* A current Australian driver's licence and willingness to undertake occasional field work and travel as required.


**Why Join RPS?**


At RPS, we believe our people are our greatest strength. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive workplace where you can develop your career while contributing to projects that create lasting value for our communities.


We offer:


* Professional development and career progression opportunities
* A supportive team culture that celebrates collaboration and success
* Flexible working arrangements to support work\-life balance
* Active wellbeing and community engagement initiatives
* Annual professional membership reimbursement
* Paid parental and partner leave
* $250 active lifestyle allowance per annum
* Additional annual leave purchase scheme and salary packaging options
* Professional and technical development programs, including study assistance, online learning and mentoring across portfolios
* Active office social events, Employee Assistance Program, service recognition and more


**Our Commitment**


At RPS, everyone is empowered to bring their best. We foster a workplace where different perspectives are valued, collaboration is encouraged and people are supported to grow professionally.


As part of Tetra Tech, we combine local knowledge with global expertise to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients while creating opportunities for our people.


Ready to Make an Impact?


If you are looking to build your environmental consulting career with a respected global consultancy and work on projects that make a real difference across Queensland and beyond, we would love to hear from you.


Apply today and help shape a more sustainable future with RPS, A Tetra Tech company.

**Our Approach**


Our people live our purpose, deliver our promise, and demonstrate our behaviours every day. Our behaviours define who we are. Developed by our people, they underpin everything that we do. They create the memorable experiences we are known for and make RPS a great place to do great work.  

Stronger together is one of our five core behaviours and it is key to building a collaborative workplace. We encourage everyone to bring their best and to support others to do the same. By sharing knowledge, challenging each other to think differently, and fostering an environment of trust and respect, our people can learn, grow and thrive – and share in our success.

**Recruitment Agencies**


We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on this list. Please refer to the careers page

jobs.location: Harris Park, New South Wales, Australia
jobs.description:
Support the Project Managers in the delivery of asbestos and Hazardous Building Materials (HBM) programs across Sydney Water's property portfolio 

Permanent full-time role based in Parramatta with hybrid working arrangements 

EA11 - $124,955.37 + super and access to Sydney Water's extensive employee benefits 

About the role 

As a Project Officer - Hazardous Materials, you will support the Project Managers in the delivery of projects and programs relating to asbestos and other Hazardous Building Materials (HBMs) across Sydney Water's land and property portfolio. Working closely with Project Managers, you will help ensure legislative compliance, manage risk, and provide technical support across a diverse range of assets and projects. Additionally, you will provide technical subject matter expertise to the business under the supervision and guidance of the Project Managers. 

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with asbestos and HBM experience who is looking to further develop their technical expertise while contributing to the safe management of critical infrastructure and property assets, ultimately creating a better life with world-class water services. 

What you will be doing 

Support the Project Managers in the delivery of Hazardous Building Materials (HBM) assessment, remediation and management projects across Sydney Water's property and building portfolio. 
Provide technical advice relating to asbestos and other HBMs in response to business and stakeholder requests across the asset lifecycle. 
Assist with the maintenance, data entry and ongoing management of HBM (Asbestos) Registers, associated databases and Sydney Water's HBM Management Plan. 
Support risk management activities by identifying, assessing and helping mitigate asbestos and HBM-related risks in accordance with legislative requirements. 
Review property and asset portfolios to identify requirements for new or updated HBM registers and assessments. 
Assist with the development of contractor project scope of services and procurement. 
Assist with the coordination and support of consultants and contractors undertaking asbestos and HBM investigations and remediation activities. 
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, business processes and Environmental Management System compliance. 
Build and maintain effective working relationships with internal stakeholders, land managers, regulators and contractors. 

About you 

You will bring technical knowledge of asbestos and hazardous building materials management, combined with strong organisational and stakeholder engagement skills. 

Ideally, you will have: 

Tertiary qualifications in Science, Safety, Occupational Hygiene or a related discipline. 
Three years or more experience in asbestos and/or HBM assessment, remediation and management. 
Experience conducting or supporting multi-site asbestos and HBM assessments and remediation programs. 
Experience in developing and implementing asbestos and other HBM management strategies, including corrective action and risk mitigations. 
Applied knowledge of relevant legislation, regulations, policies and industry standards relating to asbestos, lead and other hazardous building materials. 
Ability to identify and manage issues and constraints associated with the planning and delivery of HBM projects. 
Experience engaging and managing consultants and contractors undertaking field-based asbestos and other HBM works. 
Strong report-writing and technical review, skills. 
Effective oral communication, negotiation and interpersonal skills needed for managing stakeholders to achieve program/project outcomes. 
Well-developed organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities. 
Ability to foster teamwork as well as work independently. 
A current driver's licence and Construction Induction White Card. 
Licensed Asbestos Assessor certification will be highly regarded. 
Industry association membership with active participation, or willingness to become involved, will be highly regarded. 

Does this sound like you? Apply now! 

Closing date: 11.59 AEST on Sunday 23rd August

We support you through the application process and can modify as needed – let us know what you need. For more information, you can contact marc.evans2@sydneywater.com.au  

Please see the job profile for the role’s full accountabilities.   

Why join us  

At Sydney Water, your work will make a real difference in people’s lives—and your own. With diverse projects and roles, you'll find ample career growth opportunities. At Sydney Water, we actively seek and celebrate diversity, equity, inclusion, and individuality, fostering a safe environment where everyone can thrive and shape impactful community projects. We offer flexible working arrangements and opportunities for career progression among our many benefits.   

Dive into Our Great Benefits:  

Competitive Remuneration: We’ll ensure that your skills and contributions are valued and rewarded appropriately.  
Hybrid Work Environment: We offer a hybrid work model that balances remote work and office collaboration, supporting our team's productivity and well-being.  
Continuous Professional Growth: We will invest in your career with leadership and development programs to propel your success.  
24/7 Wellbeing Support: Access for you and your family to free and confidential mental health and general health support through our EAP portal.  
Discounted Private Health Insurance: Unlock affordable access to top-tier health coverage with our discounted insurance plans.  
Family First: Prioritise your family with up to 18 weeks of fully paid parental leave and a childcare allowance.  
Fitness Passport: Achieve your physical fitness goals using our Fitness Passport, granting you access to a multitude of gyms and pools across NSW.  
Novated Leasing: Get in the driver's seat of your financial future with our novated lease options.  

As part of the application process, Sydney Water will be collecting your personal information to assess your suitability for the role. Your personal information may also be used to establish a Dayforce talent profile. Your personal information will be collected in accordance with Dayforce’s Terms and Privacy Policy and Sydney Water’s Privacy Collection Statement – recruitment. Please note as part of the application process, you will be asked to undergo background checks which include a criminal history check.

Job Posting: Air Pollution Specialist



State Air Resources Board

Air Pollution Specialist

**Final Filing Date:** **8/25/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


The California Air Resources Board (CARB) is seeking a motivated, innovative, and technically oriented individual to join our multidisciplinary team of scientists and engineers. This position plays a critical role in developing, maintaining, and enhancing CARB’s emissions inventories, which support State Implementation Plans (SIPs), community health initiatives, regulatory development, and air quality planning across California.  

The Emissions Inventory Section is responsible for maintaining and updating CARB’s statewide criteria pollutant and toxic air contaminant inventories. Staff work closely with California’s 35 air districts to collect stationary source emissions data required under state and federal regulations. The team also collaborates with CARB’s internal programs and local districts to gather emissions data for area wide, mobile source, and event categories. Using growth and control factors developed with district partners and CARB technical teams, the section forecasts emissions inventories to future years to support air quality modeling and planning.  

To improve data quality and accessibility, the section develops and maintains applications for emissions data collection, data management, and reporting. These tools provide communities, air districts, regulators, researchers, state agencies, and other stakeholders with reliable, transparent, and user friendly emissions data.  

This position serves a vital function in the section’s work by compiling and performing rigorous quality assurance on emissions inventories submitted by local air districts and internal CARB programs. The incumbent will collaborate closely with the team’s lead forecaster to develop control profiles informed by emerging regulations and new control technologies. In addition, the position will be responsible for creating analytical tools and summary reports to evaluate emissions inventory forecasts used for air quality modeling and planning. The incumbent will also prepare standardized documentation outlining internal procedures for updating emissions inventories and control profiles. Finally, the role involves working with CARB staff, other government agencies, and academic partners to apply advanced QA/QC methods and strengthen the overall accuracy and reliability of CARB’s emissions data.  

The work produced by this section is foundational to improving air quality statewide. In this position, you will directly support air quality planning, photochemical modeling, regulatory development, community level emission reduction strategies, and project level environmental assessments. Your contributions will help ensure the accuracy and reliability of emissions data used to guide California’s most important air quality and public health decisions.  

The ideal candidate will have a strong scientific and technical background in one or more of the following areas: emissions forecasting, air quality, air quality modeling, emissions inventory development, stationary source emissions, or a closely related field. Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, collaborative capabilities, and comfort working with large datasets are highly desirable.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


This position may be eligible for hybrid in\-office work and in\-state telework. The amount of telework is at the agency's discretion and is based on the California Air Resources Board’s (CARB) current telework policy. While the CARB may support telework, some in\-person attendance is also required.

Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. The following responsibilities apply to both levels, with Level II expected to operate with greater independence and take on additional ownership:

Execute environmental monitoring programs across facilities and utilities, including viable and non-viable air and gas sampling, surface sampling, water sampling and testing, and personnel monitoring.
Perform sterility and endotoxin testing on drug product and other compendial microbiological tests as required.
Perform bioburden and endotoxin testing on incoming raw materials.
Conduct aerobic and anaerobic plate count readouts, interpret results, and generate associated reports.
Carry out media growth promotion testing, gram staining, and isolate preparation for organism identification.
Perform TOC testing of water samples using applicable instrumentation.
Enter, monitor, and trend data within a LIMS platform; assemble EM reports and provide regular updates on environmental trends to management.
Support out-of-specification investigations and microbiology-related deviations.
Maintain laboratory operations in a GMP-compliant state, coordinating with internal and external partners to ensure adequate supplies and properly functioning equipment.
Collect metrics to support continuous improvement initiatives within areas of responsibility.

Review and revise SOPs and support the document change control process.
Provide management with regular trend analysis and environmental monitoring summaries.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Microbiology or a related life sciences field; Microbiology preferred.
Minimum 2 years of experience in a QC Microbiology laboratory within a regulated environment; equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.

Familiarity with GMP, SOPs, and quality control processes.
Experience with sterile gowning, aseptic technique, and cleanroom operations a plus.
Experience with LIMS platforms (e.g. MODA) and TOC instrumentation (e.g. Sievers M9s) a plus.

Level II

Minimum 3 years of experience in a QC Microbiology laboratory within a regulated environment.
Demonstrated experience with environmental monitoring techniques including viable/non-viable air and gas monitoring, water bioburden testing, surface sampling, and personnel monitoring.
Hands-on experience with core microbiological techniques: aseptic technique, media growth promotion, microbial enumeration, gram staining, and isolate handling.

Both Levels

Proficient in MS Office Suite
Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to collaborate effectively across QC and Manufacturing teams
Ability to prioritize and manage workload independently in a dynamic, fast-paced environment
Must be authorized to work in the United States

Through the collective expertise of our nearly 26,000 employees, we operate a world\-class network of production, distribution, and ag retail facilities. We efficiently serve growers' needs and strive to provide a more profitable, sustainable, and secure future for all stakeholders. Help us raise the expectation of what an agriculture company can be and grow your career with Nutrien.

 **This individual contributor role is responsible for assessing agricultural product chemical hazard classifications, authoring safety data sheets (SDS), maintaining SDS document inventories and access systems. The position is accountable for providing a variety of internal advisory services regarding product hazard reduction options (alternate ingredients), toxicology data interpretation, and product risk matters.**

  


**What You'll Do:**
-------------------

 **Author SDSs \- Information Gathering and Documentation**

* Conduct chemical hazard assessments of new and existing chemical products (i.e., basic chemicals, fertilizers, pesticides, adjuvants) and mixtures thereof per Global Harmonzied System (GHS) and country\-specific classification requirements

* Consider appropriate regulatory requirements beyond chemical hazard classification to ensure all relevant designations and warning statements are present and correct on the SDS and/or related documents (i.e., EPA, SARA, IARC, Proposition 65\)
* Interpret lab reports for information that may affect a product hazard designation and take appropriate follow\-up action
* Develop and maintain classification weight\-of\-evidence files
* Monitor chemical hazard classification regulatory changes for impacts to Nutrien SDSs (North America)
* Acquire and maintain supporting files upon which classifications and exemptions are based, following procedures and standards for record retention
	+ Gather product information such as formulations and raw material SDSs
* Identify potential for chemical reactions and validate key reaction products with Research \& Development
* Review draft SDSs and fine\-tune output on a weight\-of\-evidence basis
* Model our core value of safety by enabling a culture in which you actively contribute to a safe work environment
* Complete other tasks and assignments to meet business objectives

 **Internal SDS Management \- Manage SDS Inventories**

* Maintain the internal site for retail SDSs
* Maintain supporting files and product documentation for accessibility and future reference
**What You'll Bring:**
----------------------

  

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Agriculture, or related field is required
* Minimum 3 years of practical experience in product hazard classifications and SDS authoring using authoring software is essential
* Ability to interpret technical data and apply weight of evidence decision making to arrive at sound and defensible classification decisions
* Aptitude for progressive learning regarding product uses e.g. fertilizers, adjuvants, pesticides, etc
* Effective written and verbal communication skills with a demonstrated ability to interact with a variety of technical functions and respond to requests with appropriate priority
* Competent knowledge of Microsoft products, primarily email, Excel, and Word
* Demonstrated analytical and problem\-solving skills to effectively solve routine problems, seeking guidance for unusual situations
* Adept at adjusting approach to work as needed
* Sound organization skills with the ability to engage in multiple initiatives at once
* Willingness to learn, teach and share information with teammates, peers, and management
* Authoring experience with industry\-standard Safety Data Sheet authoring platforms preferred but not required
* Prior work experience in safety data sheet authoring and classification using the Globally Harmonized System of Classification (GHS) preferred but not required
* Travel requirements: 0 \- 10%
 **Compensation \& Benefits:**

  

The salary range for this role, in Colorado location, is between $79,100 \- $124,190, in California location, is $79,100 \- $124,190 and between in Illinois location, is $75,300 \- $118,250\. While we provide this range as general guidance, several factors are taken into consideration when making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, candidate skill set, experience and training, licensure and certifications, work location, and other business and organizational needs. Actual salary and benefits may differ based upon location.

  

We provide an attractive benefits package that includes comprehensive medical, dental, vision coverage, and life insurance and well as disability coverage for positions working more than 30 hours per week. In addition, we have a retirement program that encourages our employees to save for the longer term, with generous matching employer contributions. Our benefit package also demonstrates our culture of care with paid vacation, sick days and holidays as well as paid personal and maternity/parental leaves and an Employee and Family Assistance Program. Details of the benefits package will be shared in the application process.

  

In addition to base pay, this role is also eligible to participate in our annual incentive plan, consistent with the terms of our program(s) where discretionary pay out of awards is reflecting components such as performance of the company and the employee. Details will be discussed through the application process.

  

This information is provided in compliance with applicable state equal pay and pay
